security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, if the illegal-instruction trap handler for U-mode WFI gates its behavior on mstatus.TW (e.g., skipping SIGILL delivery when TW=0 under the assumption that U-mode WFI is permitted), the handler would incorrectly suppress a mandatory exception. The spec now makes it unambiguous: U-mode WFI always raises illegal-instruction regardless of TW, so any TW-conditional WFI handling for U-mode is a spec violation.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: mstatus.TW checked in U-mode WFI trap handling path; or any code that conditionally permits U-mode WFI execution (e.g., do_notify_resume / exit_to_usermode_loop paths checking WFI permissiveness)
security_spec.summary: WFI in U-mode unconditionally raises illegal-instruction; mstatus.TW controls only S-mode WFI trapping — kernel must never consult TW when handling a U-mode WFI trap

findings.finding: U-mode illegal-instruction traps (including WFI) unconditionally deliver SIGILL with no mstatus.TW check. The handler calls riscv_v_first_use_handler() for lazy vector context, then falls through to do_trap_error(SIGILL). There is no code path that inspects or gates on mstatus.TW, so U-mode WFI is never incorrectly permitted.

No SR_TW or MSTATUS_TW define exists anywhere in the kernel. The only TW bit is HSTATUS_VTW (bit 21 in hstatus, CSR 0x600), which is a hypervisor CSR controlling VS-mode WFI virtualization — completely unrelated to native U-mode mstatus.TW behavior. The kernel has zero awareness of mstatus.TW.

KVM virtual-instruction fault (caused by HSTATUS_VTW trapping VS-mode WFI) is handled by kvm_riscv_vcpu_virtual_insn(), which emulates WFI by halting the VCPU. This is VS-mode (guest S-mode) WFI virtualization, not U-mode. There is no mstatus.TW check in this path, and no U-mode WFI suppression logic.

KVM WFI emulation (wfi_insn) halts the VCPU when no events are pending. This is triggered by virtual-instruction faults from VS-mode WFI when HSTATUS_VTW=1. No mstatus.TW check, no U-mode WFI conditional logic.

The return-to-userspace path (irqentry_exit_to_user_mode) contains no WFI-related logic. There is no do_notify_resume or exit_to_usermode_loop in this kernel tree, and no conditional WFI handling or emulation anywhere in the userspace entry/exit paths.
